note: Change a level here (A1–C2); the daily tasks read it before writing. English, German and French come Monday to Friday; the weekend is for review. French: two articles a day, one easier and one harder, levels rotating by weekday. Spanish (Latin American) for a friend: two items Monday to Friday, levels by weekday in levels.es.

themes.Wed: Visual culture, ISO week mod 4: contemporary art / photography / architecture & cities / film
themes.Thu: Odd ISO weeks: books & ideas; even: humanities, nature & science

themes.Wed: Kunst / Fotografie / Architektur & Design / Film & Serien (ISO-Woche mod 4)
themes.Thu: Ungerade ISO-Wochen: Bücher & Lesen; gerade: Natur & Wissen

de.tone: leicht, neugierig, feuilletonistisch; keine politischen Nachrichten, keine Lokalnachrichten

topics: world curiosities — especially East Asia, South Asia, Africa, Latin America
fr.note: Left-leaning magazines go in the 'Lectures' list as link-only reading suggestions; never copy or closely paraphrase. Paywalled pieces: link and say so, never bypass.

themes.Sat: Culture du thé / Le monde en petit / Nature (rotation)

schedule.pt: Exactly two Portuguese items a day. Mon/Thu/Sun: A1 diary + dialogue. Tue/Fri: A1 diary + Textinho. Wednesday: A1 diary + one B1/B2 crônica (for a heritage-speaker friend). Saturday: no diary — 'Histórias de canções', one song story in an A1 and a B1/B2 version.
schedule.picks: Mon–Fri: exactly 2 links per list (de, en)
schedule.weekend: Saturday and Sunday: no new English, German or French texts (no weekly review).
schedule.es: Mon–Fri around 18:00: 2 items, Latin American Spanish (ustedes, no vosotros) — one reading (culture, feminism, everyday life) and one conversation dialogue (small talk, asking questions, directions), levels rotating A1–B2 by weekday, with a short grammar note. Helper languages: English, German, Portuguese.
schedule.limit: Every language at most two items a day (picks lists don't count).

pt_focus.format: Two items every day (see schedule.pt): the Diário da Ana (first-person diary, full date, clock times, today's weekday focus) on every day except Saturday, plus ONE second item — a short everyday dialogue (Mon/Thu/Sun), a very short real-life text "Textinho" (Tue/Fri, 40–90 words), the B1/B2 crônica (Wed, separate task) or, on Saturday, the two song-story versions (separate task) instead of the diary. New glossary words of the day go into the flashcards (data/pt-BS.json).

topics_by_weekday.Mon: datas, horas e dias da semana + perguntas sobre estudos e profissão
topics_by_weekday.Tue: adjetivos e locuções adjetivas: concordância (o bolo gostoso, a casa amarela, os gatos pretos), posição depois do substantivo, substantivo + de + substantivo (bolo de chocolate, suco de laranja, casa de praia, comida de mãe) vs. de + artigo para posse (o bolo da mãe); + plural e masculino/feminino
topics_by_weekday.Wed: números (contando em português: idades, preços, telefones, horários)
topics_by_weekday.Sun: preposições (em, de, para, com, a, por + contrações no, na, do, da)

learned: dates, months, days of the week, time
Adjetivos e locuções adjetivas (substantivo + de + substantivo)

dialogue_focus.topic: perguntas: pronomes interrogativos (que / o que, quem, onde, de onde, aonde, quando, como, qual / quais, quanto / quanta / quantos / quantas, por que vs. porque, a que horas, com quem, para quem) + yes/no questions with rising intonation, "né?", "Tudo bem?"
dialogue_focus.note: Until this date the dialogue (and the Textinho, where natural) practises asking questions instead of the weekday topic; the diary keeps the weekday topic. After it, the dialogue follows topics_by_weekday again.

textinho_rotation.Tue: rotate by ISO week number mod 3 — 0: mensagens de WhatsApp entre amigos; 1: um bilhete ou recado (na geladeira, para a vizinha); 2: um convite (aniversário, festa, jantar)
textinho_rotation.Fri: rotate by ISO week number mod 3 — 0: um cardápio ou uma lista de preços; 1: uma placa ou um aviso (na padaria, no prédio, no metrô); 2: um cartão-postal ou uma agenda da semana

es_focus.who: A friend at A2 who wants to talk to people; material A1–B2, most of it A2–B1.
readings_rotate: Latin American culture & customs (one country at a time: México, Colombia, Argentina, Chile, Perú, Cuba, Guatemala, Bolivia, Uruguay, Ecuador…)
feminism & women in Latin America (movements, writers, artists, everyday questions — factual, no invented quotes)
día a día: food, markets, buses, family, work, festivals, money, apartments, weather
dialogues_rotate: small talk (meeting people, plans, hobbies, weather, compliments)
asking questions (in a shop, at a café, at the doctor's, at a hostel, on the phone)
directions (on foot, by bus/metro, asking twice, understanding landmarks)
grammar_path: perífrasis: ir a, acabar de, estar + gerundio
es_focus.easter_eggs: each item may end with a small 'dato curioso' or a regional word (e.g. México vs Argentina vs Colombia) — true facts only.
